{{Short description|Mathematical conference in Moscow (1935)}}
[[File:ETH-BIB-First International Topology Conference in Moscow-Portr 07561.tiff|thumb|right|Attendees of the First International Topological Conference, Moscow, 4–10 September, 1935]]
The '''first International Topological Conference''' was held in [[Moscow]], 4–10 September, 1935. With presentations by topologists from 10 different countries it constituted the first genuinely international meeting devoted to [[topology]] in the world history of the mathematical community.<ref name="ANS">{{cite arXiv |last1=Apushkinskaya |first1=D.E. |last2=Nazarov |first2=A. I. |last3=G.I. Sinkevich |first3=G. I. |title=In Search of Shadows: the First Topological Conference, Moscow 1935 |eprint=1903.02065 |class=math.HO |year=2019 }}</ref> Although a previous mathematical conference had been held in [[Kharkiv]], and attended by [[Jacques Hadamard]], this turned out to be the only truly international conference organised under the [[History of the Soviet Union (1927–1953)|Stalin regime]].<ref name="Weil">{{cite book |last1=Weil |first1=Andre |title=The Apprenticeship of a Mathematician |date=1992 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=9783764326500 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=73REHmJ9JNUC&dq=%22First+International+Topological+Conference%22&pg=PA106 |language=en}}</ref> [[Pavel Aleksandrov]] played a key role in organising the conference.<ref name="ANS"/> The foreign delegates were accommodated in major hotels across Moscow, although according to [[André Weil]], the principal form of sustenance was Caviar Canapes served in the conference hall, as no food was available in the hotel restaurants.<ref name="Weil"/>

==Presentations==
Documentation of the conference varies, but this summary was drawn from various sources.<ref name="ANS"/>
===Homology theory===
* Karol Borsuk: ‘‘On spheroidal spaces’’
* Eduard Čech: "Accessibility and Homology'"
* Israel Isaakovich Gordon: ‘‘On the intersection invariants of a complex and its residual space.’
* Solomon Lefschetz: ‘‘On locally connected sets.’’
